A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FiPS and retain the same core compression framework. All 16 pages of v3 and 25 pages of v4, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison despite extensive rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: V3 reports original vision accuracy, transfer-learning, LLM perplexity, ablation, latency and memory results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains original vision experiments and reports expanded LLM evaluations, quantization results and grouping sweeps, including Tables 3, 4, 6 and 8.

M1.justification: The SVD initialization, shared basis, sparse projections, block-wise reconstruction objective and optional RigL fine-tuning remain unchanged in Algorithm 1. V4 adds a FiPS-plus-QAT variant; its expanded rank and initialization explanations otherwise document the existing procedure.

E1.justification: V3 evaluates LLMs only through WikiText-2 perplexity. V4 adds C4 evaluation, six classification benchmarks and two generation tasks, TruthfulQA and GSM8K. The vision datasets and SlimPajama calibration coverage are retained.

E2.justification: V3's LLM comparison uses plain SVD and uncompressed models. V4 reports comparisons against ASVD, SVD-LLM and SVD-LLM V2, plus Basis Sharing for Llama-7B, and adds QAT-only comparators. The established vision and sparsification comparator sets largely remain.

E3.justification: LLM evaluation moves from 50%/60% MLP parameter budgets to reported 20%/40% whole-model compression, with new storage accounting and downstream metrics. Checkpoints, learning rates and groupings change: Llama-3.1-8B moves from four eight-block groups to [4,6,6,6,6,4]. QAT introduces additional precision settings. The calibration token count and 40-epoch duration remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds targeted LLM grouping sensitivity studies in Appendix A.8.1, including the five-configuration Gemma sweep in Table 8, and examines compatibility with QAT. Most existing vision ablations and sensitivity analyses are retained or rearranged. The separate FC-2 reconstruction-error panel is removed, although its qualitative conclusion remains.

E5.justification: V4 Figure 7 newly identifies timing bands as plus or minus one standard deviation over repeated measurements collected with blocked_autorange. V3 provides no corresponding statistical explanation. This does not establish an increase in run counts; accuracy and perplexity still lack comparable uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The preliminary LLM result set is replaced and substantially expanded, including downstream scores, grouping results and QAT perplexities of 35.43 versus 41.86 at reported 8× compression. Table 1 adds 75%-budget entries and changes Swin-L GFM at 50% from 85.33 to 85.44 and DeiT-B FiPS+FT at 40% from 81.55 to 81.54. Changed LLM settings prevent direct cross-version performance-gain claims.

T1.justification: V4 introduces storage/compression equations and an explicit budget-to-rank formula, and corrects the sign of the reconstruction-error increase in Section 2.3. No theorem or proof is added. The new Appendix Equation 4 nevertheless reports a remaining-size fraction, conflicting with Section 2's definition as one minus that fraction.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion replace MLP-reduction and negligible-perplexity claims with whole-model compression claims, superiority over contemporary SVD baselines and broader downstream performance. FiPS combined with QAT at reported 8× compression becomes a central contribution, whereas quantization was future work in v3.

C2.justification: V4 clarifies that overcomplete bases are not low-rank or orthogonal and that compression can instead arise from sharing and sparsity. It explains tapered grouping, conditions anticipated LLM inference gains on kernel availability, and explicitly acknowledges substantial QAT degradation relative to the uncompressed BF16 baseline.

D1.justification: V4 adds an explicit rank-selection rule, bit/mask accounting, a reproducible grouping heuristic and selection procedure, and timing software and warmup details. It also updates LLM checkpoint links, learning rates and reported compression times. These substantially expand construction and measurement documentation, although the QAT implementation remains underspecified.

R1.justification: Related work expands around ASVD, SVD-LLM, SVD-LLM V2 and concurrent Basis Sharing. V4 explicitly distinguishes FiPS from dense-coefficient sharing, ALBERT, MiniViT and methods using LoRA or distillation, repositioning novelty around the joint combination of sharing, factorization and sparsity. Several older background and calibration references are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contributions and substantial portions of the method, results, related work and conclusion are rewritten. Appendices A and B become an expanded A.1–A.9 structure, several analyses move between the main text and appendix, and the duplicated sparsity-distribution paragraph is removed.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column journal layout. Figures 4–5 redistribute retained panels; Figure 3 replaces dual accuracy axes with a broken axis; the correlation plot switches from density to sparsity; and the memory panel becomes Figure 8. Tables are moved and restructured, with new LLM, QAT and grouping displays.

improvement.justification: Modern LLM comparisons, downstream evaluation and grouping sweeps strengthen evidence that was preliminary in v3. Clearer factorization explanations and timing statistics also help. These benefits are tempered by conflicting compression definitions, inconsistent SVD-LLM V2 C4 values in Tables 3 and 6 (10.47 versus 11.72), and missing QAT implementation details, limiting the net quality gain.
